identity.title: On the Nature of the Compact Sources in IRAS 16293-2422 Seen at Centimeter to Submillimeter Wavelengths

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present multi-epoch continuum observations of the Class 0 protostellar system IRAS 16293–2422 taken with the Very Large Array (VLA) at multiple wavelengths between 7 mm and 15 cm

question.value: What is the nature of the compact sources (A1, A2, A2alpha/beta, B) in IRAS 16293-2422, based on their radio-to-submillimeter spectra, sizes, variability and proper motions?

evidence.quote: the exact number of protostars within IRAS 16293–2422, their relative evolutionary stages, and their relationship with known radio sources and outflows in the system, remain elusive.

findings_qualitative.value: Source B emission is dust-dominated down to 2 GHz and shows no excess free-free; B does not drive a powerful ionized outflow

evidence.quote: We conclude that source B does not drive a powerful ionized outflow.

claims.hypothesis: Is source B's emission dust-dominated across the whole radio-to-submm range?
claims.experiment: Combined VLA and ALMA flux densities fitted by a power law

evidence.quote: suggesting that the emission is entirely dominated by dust even at $\lambda$ = 10 cm

claims.hypothesis: Is B a finite dusty structure becoming optically thick?
claims.result: Size increases up to ~41 GHz then constant at 0.39 arcsec
claims.finding: Optically thick at mm wavelengths, central T at least ~1000 K

evidence.quote: We interpret this as evidence that source B is a dusty structure of finite size that becomes increasingly optically thick at higher frequencies

claims.hypothesis: Is A2 a protostar driving ejections, and what is A1?
claims.result: A2alpha/beta move symmetrically from A2; A1-A2 position angle began to decrease
claims.finding: A2 is a protostar; A1 nature remains open (shock feature or hierarchical triple)

evidence.quote: The new VLA observations confirm that source A2 is a protostar driving episodic mass ejections
